Routing notes:

- Option C (“regional office”) is invalid for these requests, even when the ticket mentions a regional office or a south/east/north region.
- Do not select C.
- Valid choices appear to be:
  - A: standard queue
  - B: priority desk
- No evidence yet establishes the rule for choosing A versus B. Use request urgency, size, wording, and any explicit priority indicators; do not infer that region or request type alone determines the desk.
- Ticket wording such as “before end of day,” repeated follow-up, or a bounced first attempt may indicate urgency, but this remains unverified.

Routing notes:

- Option C (“regional office”) is invalid for these requests, regardless of region or wording. Never select C.
- Valid choices are A (standard queue) and B (priority desk).
- Recent outcomes confirm that both A and B are used; neither is universally correct.
- Region, request type (claim, shipment, invoice, refund), size, sender team, and wording alone do not establish the correct desk.
- Urgency signals—“before end of day,” repeated follow-up, or a bounced first attempt—may matter, but recent results do not reliably validate a simple urgency-only rule.
- “No rush” does not guarantee A; large or routine-looking requests may still require B.
- Continue treating each ticket as a classification problem. Use explicit priority indicators first, then urgency and context, but avoid inferring from region or request category alone.
- Preserve the exact ticket features and selected option for future feedback; the latest sequence is insufficient to derive a dependable A-versus-B rule.

Routing notes:

- Option C (“regional office”) is invalid for these requests. Never select C.
- Only A (standard queue) and B (priority desk) are valid.
- Do not use region, request type, size, sender team, or wording alone as a universal rule.
- Recent labeled outcomes:
  - A correct: REQ-2426 (large shipment, north, bounced first attempt); REQ-2429 (small refund, north, bounced attempt); REQ-2430 (large shipment, north, regional-office wording); REQ-2431 (small claim, east, end-of-day wording); REQ-2432 (small refund, north, regional-office wording).
  - B correct: REQ-2427 (small shipment, north, bounced attempt); REQ-2428 (small shipment, east, end-of-day wording); REQ-2433 (small refund, east, repeated follow-up); REQ-2434 (large claim, south, end-of-day wording); REQ-2435 (small claim, north, “no rush”).
- These results directly contradict simple rules such as “bounce,” “before end of day,” or “no rush” always meaning B or A. Even near-identical tickets can differ.
- Treat each ticket as a classification problem. Consider explicit priority indicators first, then sender/team, request type, region, size, and exact wording, but avoid relying on any single feature.
- Preserve the complete feature set and selected option for every ticket; the current examples are insufficient to derive a dependable A-versus-B rule.

Routing notes:

- Option C (“regional office”) is invalid. Use only A (standard queue) or B (priority desk).
- Do not apply universal rules based on region, request type, size, sender/team, or wording. Explicit priority signals matter, but exact combinations and sender/team context can change the answer.
- Labeled outcomes:
  - A: REQ-2426 large shipment/north/bounced/unknown sender; REQ-2429 small refund/north/bounced; REQ-2430 large shipment/north/regional-office wording; REQ-2431 small claim/east/end-of-day; REQ-2432 small refund/north/regional-office.
  - B: REQ-2427 small shipment/north/bounced; REQ-2428 small shipment/east/end-of-day; REQ-2433 small refund/east/repeated follow-up; REQ-2434 large claim/south/end-of-day; REQ-2435 small claim/north/no rush.
  - REQ-2436 A: Marcus Alvarez, Client Services, small refund/north/regional-office wording.
  - REQ-2437 A: Omar Moreau, Partner Accounts, small shipment/north, “same as last month.”
  - REQ-2438 B: Jonas Moreau, Client Services, large invoice/east/end-of-day.
  - REQ-2439 A: Elena Larsen, Client Services, large claim/south, scanned-not-typed.
  - REQ-2440 A: Omar Moreau, Client Services, large claim/east, “same as last month.”
  - REQ-2441 A: Elena Haddad, Finance Desk, small claim/south/no rush.
  - REQ-2442 A: Yuki Patel, Finance Desk, large claim/south/end-of-day.
  - REQ-2443 B: Omar Haddad, Partner Accounts, large refund/east, missing-info wording.
  - REQ-2444 B: Dana Berg, Field Sales, small invoice/north/end-of-day.
  - REQ-2445 A: Marcus Haddad, Finance Desk, large shipment/north/no rush.
- Classify each ticket holistically; preserve sender, team, type, region, size, wording, and selected option. Current data still does not establish a dependable simple A/B rule.

Routing notes:

- Option C (“regional office”) is invalid. Use only A (standard queue) or B (priority desk).
- Do not infer a universal rule from region, request type, size, sender, team, or wording. Classify holistically; explicit urgency signals and sender/team context matter.
- Confirmed outcomes:
  - A: REQ-2426, 2429, 2430, 2431, 2432, 2436, 2437, 2439, 2440, 2441, 2442, 2445, 2447, 2448, 2449, 2450, 2452, 2453, 2455.
  - B: REQ-2427, 2428, 2433, 2434, 2435, 2438, 2443, 2444, 2446, 2451, 2454.
- New evidence:
  - Repeated follow-up/client asking twice can be B, but is not decisive: REQ-2446 B and REQ-2454 B; REQ-2449 and 2450 A.
  - “Same as last month” was A for REQ-2447, consistent with earlier A cases.
  - “Let me know if anything is missing” varied: A for REQ-2448 and 2452–2453, but B for REQ-2455.
  - “No rush” is not always A: REQ-2451 was B, while similar cases include A.
- Preserve all available attributes (sender, team, type, region, size, wording) and select only A or B. Current data still does not support a dependable simple rule.

Routing notes:

- Option C (“regional office”) is invalid. Use only A (standard queue) or B (priority desk).
- Classify holistically; do not infer a universal rule from region, request type, size, sender/team, or wording. Explicit urgency, follow-up history, and sender/team context may matter.
- Confirmed outcomes:
  - A: REQ-2426, 2429, 2430, 2431, 2432, 2436, 2437, 2439, 2440, 2441, 2442, 2445, 2447, 2448, 2449, 2450, 2452, 2453, 2456 (large invoice, Ingrid Patel/Partner Accounts, east, regional-office wording), 2458 (large refund, Aisha Moreau/Regional Ops, south, second attempt).
  - B: REQ-2427, 2428, 2433, 2434, 2435, 2438, 2443, 2444, 2446, 2451, 2454, 2455, 2457 (small shipment, Elena Novak/Regional Ops, east, regional-office wording), 2459 (small shipment, Omar Patel/Client Services, south, client asked twice).
- Repeated follow-up/client asking twice can be B, but is not decisive: 2446, 2454, and 2459 were B; 2449 and 2450 were A.
- “Same as last month” was A (2447).
- “Let me know if anything is missing” varied: A (2448, 2452–2453), B (2455).
- “No rush” is not always A: 2451 was B.
- Some duplicate trial records for REQ-2459 show contradictory rejections despite accepted B; retain the accepted result, but treat it cautiously.
- Preserve sender, team, type, region, size, and wording; current data supports no dependable simple rule.
